$comment: THE INTEGRITY LEDGER — what has actually been checked, when, and against what code.
WHY IT IS A LEDGER AND NOT A COMPUTATION. Every check below is an operational script
guarded by RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_ID: it refuses to run outside a deployment, and it needs the
database and the chain. Recomputing them at PR time is impossible by construction, not
merely expensive. So a run RECORDS itself here, and the board RENDERS this file.
STALENESS IS THE ONLY THING COMPUTED AT PR TIME, and it reuses the discipline the
codebase already trusts: a Level 5 verdict is stale when the inputs it judged have moved,
and a check's result is stale when the code it exercised has moved. `dependsOn` declares
that code; the board diffs it against `lastRun.commit`.
`outcome` is the ONE human input, declared once per check rather than re-judged each run:
an exit code alone cannot say whether a non-zero exit is a failure. forensics:audit-anchors
exits 5 on a corpus whose legacy anchors are not yet superseded, and that is CORRECT.
NEVER write a lastRun that was not observed. `null` means nobody has recorded a run — which
is an honest state and the whole point of the board. Stamping a believed value here would be
the same defect as backfilling anchoredHash from the column the code happens to anchor.

outcomeMeanings.CLEAN: Ran to completion and everything it checks held.
outcomeMeanings.PASS_WITH_KNOWN_LEGACY: Non-zero exit that is CORRECT: the failures it reports are legacy state explicitly out of this level's scope.
outcomeMeanings.FINDING: Ran and found something real. Not a failure of the check — a result.
outcomeMeanings.BLOCKED: Cannot pass for a reason outside the check itself.
outcomeMeanings.UNRECORDED: May have run before this ledger existed. Not evidence either way.
